subject: Intermittent 429s impacting background indexing - mitigation, evidence, and credit request
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@cloudbridge.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: CloudBridge SRE <sre@cloudbridge.io>, nina.park@cloudbridge.io
Date: 2028-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s on indexing - urgent

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing intermittent 429s on our nightly indexing job starting ~2028-03-13 23:40 UTC. The job does a steady stream of short requests (~50ms) but ~15% of requests returned 429s for ~40 minutes; it caused the backlog to grow and one downstream pipeline timed out.

Attached is a small sample of the request/response log with timestamps and request ids (throttle_log_excerpt.csv). Can you confirm whether this is a tenant-side quota spike or something on Redwood's enforcement layer? We need: 1) short-term mitigation (we can accept a temporary lift until midnight PST) 2) a postmortem + evidence for our audit team 3) an estimate for service credit/invoice adjustment.

Appreciate quick lane on this — Ari
CloudBridge - Engineering
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-14T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s on indexing - urgent

Hi Ari — thank you for the sample and ping. Really sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating this now and will keep you posted with both short and longer-term remediation.

Quick summary from initial triage:
- We confirmed a burst of 429s affecting your tenant between 2028-03-13T23:38:00Z and 2028-03-14T00:20:00Z.
- Root cause (initial): an enforcement-window mapping error where a recently created tenant alias did not inherit your configured burst window. That caused requests that should have been in a 60s rolling window to be evaluated under the default 10s enforcement window.

Immediate steps we've taken:
- Temporary routing change applied to CloudBridge tenant at 09:20 PDT to route to a permissive policy, which should eliminate the 429s while we push a configuration fix.
- We're preparing a patch to normalize enforcement-window inheritance for aliases; Ben is prepping the diff.

Proposed next steps for today:
1) We'll keep the permissive route in place until 23:59 PST unless you ask us to revert earlier.
2) I'll send you an evidence bundle (logs, token counts, policy eval traces) by EOD.
3) We'll propose a service credit for the impacted window; preliminary estimate below.
4) Schedule a 30-minute technical sync today to walk through the logs and the patch plan.

Can you confirm a time for a quick call (I have availability 10:30–11:30 or 15:00–16:30 PST)? We aim to avoid any disruption to your indexing.

Attachments referenced: throttle_log_excerpt.csv

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s on indexing - urgent (internal)

Kimberly — internal tech note / proposed remediation: 
- Root cause confirmed: enforcement-window inheritance missing for alias 'cb-indexing-legacy' introduced 2028-03-02. Enforcement policy evaluator fell back to default window (10s) causing burst thresholds to trigger at typical indexing rates.
- Fix: small patch to enforcement service that ensures tenant-level window configuration is applied to aliases. Patch file: enforcement-window-fix.patch (attached).
- Deployment plan: staged rollout to hostpool A (non-prod) for verification, then hostpool B (prod read path) with a quick config flip. Expect ~10 minutes to push and verify; we'll keep permissive route until verification completes.
- Risk: low; change is configuration inheritance only, no kernel/runtime model changes.

I'll own the rollout with Vanessa for monitoring. After deploy we'll collect policy-eval traces and produce the evidence bundle for CloudBridge and for your audit request.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@cloudbridge.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: CloudBridge SRE <sre@cloudbridge.io>, nina.park@cloudbridge.io
Date: 2028-03-14T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s on indexing - urgent

Thanks Kimberly — confirm we've seen the error rate drop since ~12:45 PDT and our indexing job has progressed. Appreciate the quick routing change.

Two asks before we close this out: 
1) Please provide the evidence bundle with the policy-eval traces and token accounting so we can forward to our compliance team.
2) Please confirm the service credit calculation and whether you can apply the credit to the March invoice (we were charged for the failed calls).

Also, can you confirm whether this configuration gap could affect other tenants with aliases created after 2028-03-01? If so, we'd like an account-wide check.

Best,
Ari
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-14T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s on indexing - urgent

Hi Ari — quick wrap here with deliverables and next steps. Thanks again for flagging this; really sorry for the disruption.

Deliverables (attached / links):
- redwood_evidence_bundle_20280314.zip (policy-eval traces, token accounting csvs, request ids crosswalk) — link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3C_example_evidence
- Patch submitted: enforcement-window-fix.patch (Jira INF-4127).
- Audit note: we've scheduled an automated scan for other tenants with aliases created after 2028-03-01; initial pass shows 12 tenants with missing inheritance flags. We'll remediate those via a bulk config job starting 2028-03-15 02:00 UTC; we'll share the runbook and results.

Service credit / billing: based on the failed token count and your committed plan, Finance proposes a one-time credit of USD 2,400 applied to the March invoice. If you prefer a pro-rated adjust instead, we can do that — let me know.

Postmortem: we've scheduled a 45-minute postmortem tomorrow 2028-03-15T10:00 PDT (invite sent to your SREs). Agenda: timeline, root cause, mitigation, compensating controls, and follow-up owners.

Immediate ask from your side: please confirm you received the evidence bundle and whether you approve the credit to apply to March invoice. If you'd like the permissive route removed earlier than midnight PST, tell us and we'll revert.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood_evidence_bundle_20280314.zip, enforcement-window-fix.patch
